title: Boundary First Audience and Use-Case Registry
description: A visitor-centered routing overlay that references, but does not replace, the canonical content graph.

intents.title: Understand the central idea
intents.prompt: I want to understand the central idea.
intents.summary: Begin with a familiar consequence, acquire the minimum vocabulary, then reveal the larger atlas.

intents.title: Diagnose a system or recurring failure
intents.prompt: I have a system or problem I need to diagnose.
intents.summary: Identify the consequential boundary, protected invariant, closure failure, consequence path, and repair responsibility.

intents.title: Use practical tools and methods
intents.prompt: I want practical tools and methods.
intents.summary: Move from domain example to field guide, worksheet, implementation pattern, and review practice.

intents.title: Evaluate or challenge the research
intents.prompt: I want to evaluate, criticize, or replicate the work.
intents.summary: Route directly to exact claims, provenance, operating domains, evidence, negative results, and reproduction materials.

intents.title: Build, collaborate, or support
intents.prompt: I want to build, collaborate, or support the lab.
intents.summary: Expose bounded programs, maturity, needs, responsibilities, and the witness artifact a collaboration should produce.

intents.title: Recover representation, agency, or repair
intents.prompt: I am looking for representation, agency, or repair.
intents.summary: Begin with lived consequence, then make the system's representation, authority, omissions, standing, and repair paths legible.

doorways.title: Software
doorways.summary: Interfaces, state, architecture, execution, and closure make the method concrete.

doorways.title: Soccer
doorways.summary: A continuous, noisy, embodied multi-agent system of constructed and repaired boundaries.

doorways.title: Chess
doorways.summary: A finite, inspectable state space for learning consequential boundaries and admissible transitions.

doorways.title: The body
doorways.summary: Modern environments, embodied constraints, self-observation, and informed maintenance.

doorways.title: Institutions
doorways.summary: Authority, standing, consequence, representation, appeal, and repair.

doorways.title: Mathematics and formal systems
doorways.summary: Exact objects, lawful transformations, invariants, closure conditions, and proof obligations.

audiences.title: The curious recognizer
audiences.arrivalStatement: I sense that this connects many things, but I do not yet have the language.
audiences.trigger: A familiar example or public idea reveals a recurring pattern.
audiences.barrier: The complete portfolio appears too large to enter.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Recognize the pattern, understand the basic method, and choose a next path.
audiences.successSignal: The visitor can state the pattern in their own words and choose a deeper route.

route.title: See a consequential boundary
route.summary: Begin with one familiar system and show what changes when a relevant distinction is omitted.

route.title: Acquire the four questions
route.summary: What is the boundary? What must remain true? Where can closure fail? Who can repair it?

route.title: Reveal the larger atlas
route.summary: Connect the familiar example to Distinction Space and Boundary Theory without requiring the whole corpus.

audiences.title: The self-directed learner
audiences.arrivalStatement: I want to become capable of understanding and using this material.
audiences.trigger: Curiosity, exclusion from a gated field, or a need to acquire practical intellectual tools.
audiences.barrier: Prerequisites and disciplinary language are implicit.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Acquire the distinctions, practice the method, and participate meaningfully.
audiences.successSignal: The learner can apply the method to a new example without copying the original wording.

route.title: Locate current knowledge
route.summary: Choose a doorway and declare what is already familiar.

route.title: Acquire vocabulary progressively
route.summary: Introduce distinctions only when the learner needs them to solve the next problem.

route.title: Apply and receive feedback
route.summary: Use exercises that expose omitted distinctions, false closure, and repair requirements.

audiences.title: The working practitioner
audiences.arrivalStatement: I am responsible for a real system, and something about it does not close.
audiences.trigger: Recurring defects, architectural disagreement, invisible manual repair, or displaced complexity.
audiences.barrier: Structural necessities are treated as taste, style, or personality.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Identify the omitted distinction, endangered invariant, broken boundary, and required repair.
audiences.successSignal: The practitioner can make the structural disagreement legible and testable.

route.title: Name the consequential system
route.summary: Bound the domain, affected actors, and claimed completion condition.

route.title: Find the closure failure
route.summary: Trace omitted states, crossed responsibilities, hidden work, and downstream consequence.

route.title: Specify repair and witness
route.summary: Declare the repaired invariant, responsible owner, test, and evidence of closure.

audiences.title: The builder and product user
audiences.arrivalStatement: I want a tool, workflow, or product that helps me perform this work.
audiences.trigger: A concrete task needs a repeatable instrument rather than another explanation.
audiences.barrier: The theory is useful but not yet operational in the current workflow.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Use or build an instrument that produces a reliable, inspectable difference.
audiences.successSignal: The tool makes a previously unreliable operation repeatable and inspectable.

route.title: Bound the job to be done
route.summary: Declare the input, output, protected invariant, failure modes, and witness.

route.title: Choose or specify the instrument
route.summary: Select the smallest tool that closes the real workflow.

route.title: Produce evidence through use
route.summary: Treat deployment and maintenance as tests of the representation.

audiences.title: The organizational leader
audiences.arrivalStatement: My organization repeatedly produces failures that no individual intervention seems to fix.
audiences.trigger: Capable people repeatedly encounter the same systemic defect.
audiences.barrier: Authority, representation, consequence, and repair are distributed across incompatible structures.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Locate the misalignment and identify the smallest consequential repair.
audiences.successSignal: The recurring failure can be traced to a repairable structural mismatch rather than blamed on individuals.

route.title: Start from consequence
route.summary: Identify who bears the result and who can observe the failure.

route.title: Map authority and responsibility
route.summary: Find where decision power and repair obligation separate.

route.title: Choose a bounded intervention
route.summary: Repair the smallest boundary that restores visibility, standing, or closure.

audiences.title: The affected participant and self-advocate
audiences.arrivalStatement: A system acts upon me, but I cannot adequately see, influence, contest, or repair its representation of me.
audiences.trigger: A consequential institutional, bodily, educational, or automated system becomes dependency-producing or illegible.
audiences.barrier: The system has a representation of the person, but the person lacks a usable representation of the system.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Identify boundaries, claims, responsibilities, omissions, standing, and available repair paths.
audiences.successSignal: The participant can ask better questions, document consequence, and locate a viable recourse path.

route.title: Begin with lived consequence
route.summary: Record what happens without requiring institutional vocabulary first.

route.title: Map the system's representation
route.summary: Identify what the system can see, what it ignores, and who can alter the record.

route.title: Find standing and repair
route.summary: Locate evidence, decision authority, appeal, maintenance, or self-care pathways.

audiences.title: The educator and translator
audiences.arrivalStatement: I see educational value here and need a reliable way to teach it.
audiences.trigger: A learner group needs a bounded, claim-safe progression.
audiences.barrier: The material is too broad to teach as a single undifferentiated theory.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Deliver an audience-appropriate sequence with clear objectives, examples, and limits.
audiences.successSignal: Learners transfer the method to new domains without mistaking the example for the theory.

route.title: Define the learner boundary
route.summary: State prior knowledge, context, time, and desired capability.

route.title: Select a familiar on-ramp
route.summary: Choose an example that reveals the operation while preserving claim limits.

route.title: Test transfer
route.summary: Ask learners to reconstruct the pattern in a different domain.

audiences.title: The formal researcher
audiences.arrivalStatement: I want to determine what is defined, novel, provable, falsifiable, or useful.
audiences.trigger: A formal object, conjecture, derivation, or interdisciplinary claim requires evaluation.
audiences.barrier: Public synthesis can obscure exact claim type, provenance, and proof obligation.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Identify the exact object, contribution, prior-art relation, and next valid test.
audiences.successSignal: The researcher can isolate and test the actual claim.

route.title: Isolate the claim
route.summary: Separate interpretation, definition, conjecture, theorem, and supported result.

route.title: Locate prior art and operating domain
route.summary: State where the object applies and which neighboring frameworks matter.

route.title: Specify the next valid test
route.summary: Expose proof obligations, counterexamples, experiments, and promotion conditions.

audiences.title: The critic, reviewer, and replicator
audiences.arrivalStatement: I want to test whether the work withstands serious scrutiny.
audiences.trigger: A consequential claim needs independent criticism or reproduction.
audiences.barrier: The actual claim is difficult to separate from surrounding rhetoric or synthesis.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Criticize or reproduce the exact claim with access to provenance, limits, and correction history.
audiences.successSignal: Agreement is unnecessary; informed criticism becomes easier and more precise.

route.title: Trace the claim
route.summary: Locate source, inference, status, operating domain, and current wording.

route.title: Stress the boundaries
route.summary: Search for compression loss, contradiction, unsupported promotion, and failure cases.

route.title: Record criticism and repair
route.summary: Preserve objections, responses, negative results, and supersession without silent reconciliation.

audiences.title: The collaborator, partner, or supporter
audiences.arrivalStatement: I see potential alignment and need to understand where I can contribute.
audiences.trigger: A program, product, funding opportunity, or institutional need appears aligned.
audiences.barrier: The lab's breadth makes the bounded opportunity difficult to see.
audiences.desiredTransformation: Understand the program architecture and a specific, responsible contribution path.
audiences.successSignal: The partner can name the bounded opportunity, contribution, risk, and expected output.

route.title: Locate genuine alignment
route.summary: Match the partner's capability and need to an active program rather than the whole lab.

route.title: Bound the collaboration
route.summary: Declare deliverable, decision rights, risk, source boundary, and review gate.

route.title: Define the witness artifact
route.summary: Specify what publication, prototype, dataset, pilot, or institutional change will demonstrate completion.
